🚨TX-28 Highlights:

$2.3M Starr County Courthouse
$1.2M La Joya Fire Station
$3.5M El Faro Road Flood Mitigation
$2M @neighborworks Laredo
$1M Zapata County EOC
$2M @cityoflaredo substance use treatment center
$2M Gateway Health Center Laredo 
$5M Roma-Miguel Aleman Intl. Bridge

I met with the Children’s Hospital Association of Texas today to discuss children's mental and behavioral health care, including how we can solve problems in the workforce and the lack of beds.
 
Thank you for your work to promote health and wellness for TX-28 families. https://t.co/DqBfLPW2Yr

September is National Recovery Month—a month to recognize all of the individuals who help our community recover from mental health and substance use disorders. 

Thank you to doctors, treatment centers, nonprofits, and the recovery community for all you do. #CongressGoesPurple https://t.co/DXhrcDQlBu

I joined @CNN to discuss the ongoing situation at our southern border.

The reality is we need the State of Texas to work with the federal government to secure the border.

https://t.co/o5yT2VHXf9

Yesterday, CMS announced that 524,909 Texas children have been disenrolled from Medicaid and CHIP, which is the highest number in the nation and makes up nearly 24% of all children who have lost Medicaid or CHIP coverage in the US since renewals began in March 2023.

(1/2)

Good news: Today, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services approved increasing postpartum #Medicaid and #CHIP coverage in Texas to 12 months after pregnancy.

An estimated 137k more Texas moms and babies will now be eligible for health care coverage post-pregnancy – a huge win for Texas! #MaternalHealth

While in Starr County this afternoon, I also announced $28,945,000 in federal funding for Union Water Supply Corporation.
 
These dollars will go towards expanding and rehabilitating a water treatment plant, ensuring South Texans have clean drinking water.
 
Thank you to Lillian Salerno, USDA Rural Development State Director, Marlene Mendoza, President of the Union Water Supply Board of Directors, and County Commissioner Eloy Garza for working with me to deliver for Starr County!

14 years ago, the Affordable Care Act was signed into law!

Since then, the #ACA has provided Americans with quality, affordable health coverage.

Let’s continue to build on this process and make health care more affordable and accessible for everyone. https://t.co/MpIGVBJNox

I am working hard to expand the VA’s presence in South Texas.

Our veterans shouldn’t have to travel for hours or wait for months to receive treatment.

I was pleased to ask @SecVetAffairs today how the VA is working to ensure every South Texas veteran has access to healthcare. https://t.co/XudZML5YKe

Great news for Rio Bravo and El Cenizo – I helped secure $10 million in federal funding for upgrades to the Rio Bravo Wastewater Treatment Plant.

These dollars come from the American Rescue Plan Act, which I helped pass into law in 2021. https://t.co/KAKioNlvWE

This afternoon, I met with Roberto Haddad with DHR Health in Edinburg.

We discussed improving health care in South Texas by supporting safety-net hospitals, which serve patients regardless of insurance status.

I will continue to fight for affordable, accessible health care in South Texas.

Today, I honored the life of Dr. Paul Raymond Buitrón, MD, for his 49 years of service to patients in Laredo and all of South Texas.

Born and raised in Laredo, he found a passion in the medical field and built strong relationships with all of his patients.

I presented his son with a Congressional Certificate of Recognition to ensure Dr. Buitrón's service to South Texas is memorialized.

Today, I announced $100,000 in grant funding for MedCognition for HAZMAT training. 

MedCognition will use this funding to research more effective training methods for HAZMAT professionals. 

Training will be centered on treating patients who have been exposed to poisonous gas, corrosive materials, and poisonous gas. 

I will continue to fight for medical treatment and advancements for our district and ensure our safety.

Today, I announced $2 million in federal funding over five years for the Veterans Treatment Program based in Webb County. 
 
This funding will benefit veterans across South Texas, including those in Webb County and five of its neighboring rural counties including Zapata, Jim Hogg, Starr, Duval, and Jim Wells. 
 
This funding will provide mental health counseling for substance abuse disorders and PTSD for over 200 veterans across South Texas.
 
I am dedicated to improving access to these crucial services and will continue advocating for our veterans in Congress.

Medicare is helping Americans, including families across TX-28, save more than ever on prescription drugs. This program is making a real difference in lowering healthcare costs and ensuring access to vital medications. 

Don’t miss your chance to get the coverage you need—Medicare Open Enrollment is open now through December 7. Visit https://t.co/PIvMkfGj10 to explore your options, compare plans, and secure the best coverage for you and your loved ones.

This afternoon, my Legislative Correspondent, Zachary Johnson, met with representatives from the Texas Organization of Rural and Community Hospitals. They discussed the presence of rural hospitals in the district and policy matters related to healthcare in Texas. I look forward to supporting them and their efforts to provide healthcare for rural Texans.

I am proud to have secured $2,000,000 in federal funding for Webb County’s Veterans Treatment Program (VTP), which I announced last year. Provided over a five-year period, this funding is expanding the Veterans Treatment Court Program to help veterans overcome substance abuse and mental health challenges through treatment, education, and rehabilitation services.

It also extends support to veterans in five neighboring rural counties—Zapata, Jim Hogg, Starr, Duval, and Jim Wells—where a lack of resources has left many without critical care. By reducing recidivism, improving mental health, and promoting public safety, this program is helping veterans build better lives.

Thank you to all the veterans in South Texas and across the nation for your service. I remain committed to ensuring you receive the care and support you deserve.

Today, I visited the Ruthe B. Cowl Rehabilitation Center and had the opportunity to see the incredible work they do to support patients on their road to recovery. RBC focuses on improving mobility, balance, and independence while helping patients recover from illness or injury.  

The center provides essential services, including physical, occupational, and speech therapy, as well as internship opportunities for future healthcare professionals. Their dedication to minimizing risks for patients and clinicians while increasing efficiency is truly commendable. I appreciate the important role they play in our community and look forward to supporting their mission.

Yesterday, I had the chance to visit the ROOTS Recovery Center, a facility I’m deeply proud to support. I secured $2,000,000 in federal funding for the City of Laredo Detoxification Center, now known as ROOTS, to ensure our community has access to the critical addiction treatment services we need. This funding supports staff salaries and essential resources, including electronic medical records, healthcare supplies, and food—resources that directly impact the care and well-being of those struggling with addiction.

During my tour, I had the opportunity to meet with patients and hear their personal stories. It was incredibly moving to witness their resilience and determination as they work toward recovery. ROOTS provides 24/7 medical detoxification services, crisis stabilization, and comprehensive support to help patients through their journey. It’s a place where people can find hope, healing, and the help they need to rebuild their lives. I’m truly committed to supporting ROOTS and the vital work they do every day to make a difference in people’s lives.

Today, my wife, Imelda, attended the ASAS Health Partners Western Theme Patient Appreciation Party! It was a fun and memorable event, bringing everyone together to celebrate and show appreciation for the wonderful patients. https://t.co/FjViZqb2XY

This week, my Laredo Outreach Coordinator Andres Velazquez attended the FITBEATS grand opening to present a Congressional Certificate of Recognition to owner Sarahi Villanueva.

Thank you for empowering women through wellness, dance, and entrepreneurship in #TX28! https://t.co/7GYKVJF1Lm

My San Antonio Outreach Coordinator, Olivia Branson celebrated the opening of the Armed Services YMCA child care facility in the BAMC waiting room—a meaningful step in supporting service members by providing child care while they receive treatment. https://t.co/cNNxtnA4Qz
Wishing President Biden strength and healing as he begins treatment. My prayers are with him and his loved ones.

Through my work on the Appropriations Committee, I fought to ensure key language was included to strengthen care for veterans facing substance use challenges.
 
This week, I helped secure $232.9 million to expand Substance Use Disorder treatment at the VA. This funding will enhance provider training and introduce new online tools to better support veterans in recovery.
 
I also helped secure funding for the creation of a new pilot program that applies advanced medical technology to reduce diabetic amputations and prevent insulin-related emergencies. These are life-saving investments for our veteran community.
 
We owe it to every veteran to deliver the best possible care, and this bill moves us closer to that promise. Proud to work alongside @DeptVetAffairs to support those who’ve served.

The Senate’s proposed tax-and-spending package is projected to add $3.3 trillion to the national deficit, while also making significant cuts to crucial federal programs like Medicaid and SNAP that many families in South Texas depend on.

These programs are lifelines in our region, providing access to health care, nutrition, and economic stability for seniors, children, and working families. Scaling them back to help fund tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans risks deepening the challenges already faced by rural communities.

We need thoughtful, fiscally responsible legislation that supports long-term growth while protecting the needs of our residents. I am committed to working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to ensure federal policy meets the real needs of #TX28.
